Atay — The Mint Tea Ceremony

Prep: 5 min · Cook: 8 min · Total: 15 min (plus the ceremony's pour) · Makes 1 pot (4–6 glasses)

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • 2 tsp gunpowder green tea (about 6 g) — the tightly-rolled pearl's smoky-honest register
  • 1 large handful fresh spearmint (about 20 g), the stems' top half — the mint's own law below
  • 3–4 tsp sugar (about 12–16 g), or the sugar cube's traditional count at the glass's edge — the atay runs sweeter than the tea-drinker's expectation, the ceremony's own honest register
  • 500 ml boiling water (about 500 g)
  • The traditional pot: the teapot's squat and the glass's ornate — the kettle's mercy at the plain kitchen's honesty

Instructions

  1. **The tea's rinse (2 minutes).** The gunpowder pearls at the pot; the boiling water's first pour — a scant half-cup (about 100 ml) — swirled at the pot's shake and poured off at once: the rinse's law washing the tea's factory dust and the bitterness's first edge, the pearls' own awakening at the hot's mercy. Checkpoint — the rinse's proof: the discarded water runs the faint amber's cloud (the dust's wash) — the tea's own color running whole at the second pour's honesty; the long-rinsed pot runs the tea's flavor's waste, and the unrinsed runs the bitter's edge at the glass's first.
  2. **The pack and the brew (5 minutes).** The mint's handful pressed at the pot (the stems' down, the leaves' crush at the pack's own release), the sugar's spoonfuls, and the boiling water's full pour to the pot's fill — the brew's steep at the 5-minute's patience, the pot set at the gentle heat's return (the barest warmth at the stove's corner, never the boil's bitter). Checkpoint — the brew's proof at the 5-minute's peek: the pot's liquid runs the amber-green's depth, the mint's dark and the tea's pearl-run at the surface's float, the perfume rising at the spout's first — the over-steeped pot runs the bitter's tannin's edge at the 8-minute's past.
  3. **The three pours' aeration — the ceremony's own technique.** The pot's pour to the first glass at the high arm's stream (the arm's full extension at the glass's rim's foot — the long fall running the aeration's oxygen at the tea's body) — and the glass's return to the pot: the pour-and-return at the three's repetition, the blend's whole marriage at the fall's mercy. Checkpoint — the aeration's proof at the third pour: the glass runs the fine foam's crown at the tea's surface — the fall's own signature at the oxygen's work — and the taste runs the blend's whole: the tea's smoky depth and the mint's bright green run the single glass's marriage, never the two flavors' side-by-side.
  4. **The service's law.** The glasses poured at the high arm's every glass (the ceremony's every pour running the aeration's repetition), the pot's refills at the water's mercy (the atay's pot runs the three glasses' honest law at the same leaves' second and third steep — the mint's fresh handful at the second's renewal). Checkpoint — eating test: the glass at the thumb-and-forefinger's rim-grip (the heat's law at the ornate glass's own honesty — the glass's burn running the ceremony's own education), the first sip's register: the sweet first (the ceremony's honest sugar), the tea's smoky-honey depth at the middle, the mint's cool-green finish running the glass's whole length. It should taste like the arrival's own greeting — the hospitality's first word and the table's last.

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The atay runs no keeping's law — the ceremony's pot is the moment's own (the refill's second steep running the same hour's economy) — and the mint's bunch keeps the week at the jar's water at the fridge's mercy.
